text: The Fed under Chair Warsh has held rates at 3.5%-3.75% for five straight meetings with nearly half of policymakers open to a hike — combined with CPI still running at 3.3% and GDP slowing to 1.5%, this means borrowing costs are staying high longer than expected, which hurts growth stocks and speculative holdings the most.

Sell RGTI — you're down 45%, revenue is shrinking by 34%, insiders are selling, 18% of traders are betting against it, and the stock is 73% off its highs, meaning the thesis here is broken and staying in is just hoping for a miracle.

Sell QBTS — you're down 41% with no path to profitability, over 20% short interest (one of the highest levels you can see), insiders are dumping shares, and speculative tech with no earnings gets punished hardest when rates stay this high.

Trim IONQ — you're down 18% and the stock is 52% off its highs with no earnings, 10.5% short interest, and quantum computing is still years from generating real revenue, so reduce your exposure and protect what's left.

Trim MSTR — while you're slightly up at 7.6%, this is a leveraged Bitcoin bet that's 60% off its highs with terrible fundamentals, and in a high-rate environment where speculation gets punished, reducing your position size here is smart risk management.

Add to UNH — at 17.7x earnings with nearly 12% revenue growth and strong cash flow, UnitedHealth is a genuine value opportunity in a slowing economy where defensive healthcare names with real profits tend to outperform.

Add to GOOGL — at 22.8x earnings with 15% revenue growth and positive free cash flow, Google is reasonably priced for a mega-cap tech leader and the kind of quality name that holds up well when the economy slows.
